lc_person: Gérard Raulet, philosopher and historian of German ideas; professor at Rennes II and Paris-Sorbonne, editor of Utopie-marxisme selon Ernst Bloch and Die Frage nach dem Subjekt.
item_person: Gérard Raulet, philosopher, translator and university teacher specializing in German philosophy, associated with Paris-Sorbonne.

evidence.says: LC identifies Raulet, Gérard through Utopie, marxisme selon Ernst Bloch (1976). Its structured birth date is 1942, following a Postmoderne (1986) note describing a Paris-Sorbonne IV teacher; another note, for Die Frage nach dem Subjekt (1988), gives 1949 and a Germanistics professorship at Rennes.
Gérard Raulet is described as a philosopher, translator and university teacher working in German philosophy, with birth year 1949; identifiers include LC n83067309, BnF 119212122 and VIAF 7396043.

The national-library authority gives birth year 1949 and identifies a philosopher specializing in the history of German philosophy, professor at Rennes II and researcher at SIRICE. It cites Weimar ou l’explosion de la modernité (1984).

The graph’s Open Library author has works including Positive Barbarei: Kulturphilosophie und Politik bei Walter Benjamin, Das Zwischenreich der symbolischen Formen, Historismus, Sonderweg und dritte Wege, and European Constitutionalism.

The institutional profile places Raulet at Paris-Sorbonne in 1975–1987, Rennes II in 1987–1994, and later as professor of German intellectual history at Paris-Sorbonne. Its bibliography matches LC’s 1976 Bloch volume and 1988 Die Frage nach dem Subjekt, and all four Open Library titles listed above.

notes: The birth discrepancy occurs within LC’s own source notes. The matching works and career identify one person; BnF supports 1949. The graph’s Open Library evidence independently matches the institutional bibliography. No replacement QID is needed.
